\chapter{Review --- The Same Six, In Use}
\label{ch:repaso-seis-en-uso}
\hlchaptermodality{336}

\begin{chapteropening}
\textbf{By the end of this chapter:} \emph{I can buy una entrada, ask for el cambio, name a bebe and a pareja, and report my calor and my edad in whole turns.}

Complete ES-C336-repaso-seis-en-uso: split tengo calor from hace calor, ask an age with the noun, and put all six inside a turn of four words or fewer.
\end{chapteropening}

\section[(review)]{Review --- the same six, inside something you would say}

\label{lesson:ES-C336-repaso-seis-en-uso}



\begin{quote}
Two from last time, in the other direction. Say \emph{heat}, then \emph{age}. (\emph{El calor}; \emph{la edad}.)
\end{quote}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
Naming a word and using it are two different acts of memory, and the second is the one you will need at a counter. So the six come round again, each sitting inside the shortest real thing it belongs to.

\emph{Mi pareja} --- my partner. \emph{El nombre del bebé} --- the baby's name. \emph{Una entrada, por favor} --- one ticket, please. \emph{¿Y el cambio?} --- and the change? \emph{Tengo calor} --- I am hot. \emph{¿Qué edad tienes?} --- how old are you?

Every one of those is four words or fewer, and every one of them is a whole turn in a conversation.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
Say these aloud:

\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{mi pareja}
  \item \emph{el nombre del bebé, por favor}
  \item \emph{una entrada, por favor}
  \item \emph{¿y el cambio?}
  \item \emph{tengo calor}
  \item \emph{¿qué edad tienes?}
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
How do you buy one way in? (\emph{Una entrada, por favor}.) How do you ask for your coins back? (\emph{¿Y el cambio?}.) How do you say the baby's name, and your own partner? (\emph{El nombre del bebé}; \emph{mi pareja}.) And two ways to report yourself? (\emph{Tengo calor}; \emph{mi edad}.)
\end{tcolorbox}
